# rimsky CLI reference

The `rimsky` binary drives a rimsky deployment from the command line. Most verbs are a thin HTTP+JSON client over the control API. A few — the `ctx` verbs, `daemon status`, `daemon stop`, `version` — run entirely on your machine and contact nothing. Two verbs, `rimsky run` and `rimsky compose run`, boot a whole rimsky stack inside the CLI process.

Read this document to find a verb, its arguments, its flags, and what it does. Read the last section, [Where the CLI will surprise you](#where-the-cli-will-surprise-you), before you script against it.

## Conventions

### Invocation

Run `rimsky <verb> [subcommand] [flags] [arguments]`. Running `rimsky` with no arguments prints the root usage to stderr and exits 2. An unknown verb prints the same usage to stderr and exits 2.

### The common flag set

Most control-API verbs share five flags:

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--endpoint <url>` | Control-API base URL for this invocation. |
| `--key <token>` | API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. |
| `-o`, `--output human\|json` | Output format. Defaults to `human`. |
| `--no-color` | Suppress ANSI color. |
| `--yes` | Stands in for `--force` on `instance kill`, and answers the compose family's prompt. |

The dev-loop verbs, the grouped literal-API verbs (`template`, `tag`, `instance`, `node`, `admin`, `parked`, `messages`, `asset`, `lineage`), `health`, `watch`, and `ctx list` take this set. The `auth`, `daemon`, `conformance`, and `compose run` families parse their own flags and reject these names. `ctx use`, `ctx add`, `ctx rm`, and `ctx current` do the same.

Flags may appear before or after positional arguments on the verbs that use the common set. Attached short values do not work: write `-o json` or `-o=json`, never `-ojson`. Clustering does not work either.

### Resolving the endpoint

The CLI picks the control-API URL from the first source that answers:

1. `--endpoint`.
2. `RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_URL`.
3. The manifest's `context:` field, on the compose verbs.
4. The context named by `RIMSKY_CONTEXT`, in `~/.rimsky/config.yml`.
5. The `current_context` recorded in `~/.rimsky/config.yml`.

With none of these set, the verb fails with `no endpoint configured: pass --endpoint, set RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_URL, or run 'rimsky ctx use <name>'` and exits 2. `rimsky run` is the exception: it reads the same chain, and treats "nothing configured" as a request to self-host.

`rimsky compose up|down|plan|status` invert the priority: a manifest that pins a `context:` wins over the environment. Passing `--endpoint` alongside a pinned context is an error unless the two resolve to the same URL.

### Resolving the API key

The CLI picks the key from the first source that answers: `--key`, then `RIMSKY_API_KEY`, then the `api_key` recorded on the active context in `~/.rimsky/config.yml`. `rimsky auth` uses the same chain under its own `--key` flag. The compose family reads neither — see [Where the CLI will surprise you](#where-the-cli-will-surprise-you).

### Contexts and the config file

`~/.rimsky/config.yml` holds named contexts, each with an `endpoint` and an optional `api_key`, plus a `current_context`. The CLI writes it with mode `0600`. Context names must start with a letter and may run up to 63 characters of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, and `-`.

### Output

`-o human` prints aligned tables and key/value blocks. `-o json` prints an indented JSON document. Anything other than `human`, `json`, `text`, or `table` is rejected with `unknown output format`.

The CLI emits color only when the destination is a terminal. `--no-color` and a non-empty `NO_COLOR` environment variable both disable it.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | The verb succeeded. |
| 1 | The request failed, or the server answered an error. |
| 2 | Usage error: a bad flag, a wrong argument count, an unknown subcommand, or an unresolvable endpoint. |

Three verbs add codes of their own. `rimsky template lint` exits 1 when the template has findings. `rimsky compose plan` exits 3 when the plan carries changes or drift warnings, and 0 when the live world already matches the manifest. `rimsky run` in self-host mode and `rimsky compose run` exit 0 on success, 1 on any instance failure, 2 on `--timeout` expiry, and 130 on SIGINT or SIGTERM.

### Referring to things

Templates take a `<ref>`: a full template hash, or a tag pointing at one. Instances take an `<id-or-key>`: the instance UUID, or the `instance_key` the creator set. Tags whose name starts with `compose:` are reserved for the compose family; the CLI refuses to create, move, or remove one.

## Dev-loop verbs

These verbs shorten the common path. Five of them dispatch straight to a grouped verb and behave identically to it, down to the flags, the output bytes, and the exit codes.

### `rimsky run {<file>|--template <name>}`

Registers a template, deploys it, creates an instance, and wakes it — in one command.

`run` chooses between two modes. When an endpoint resolves, it drives that deployment remotely. When nothing resolves, it boots an in-process all-in-one stack on a loopback port, drives the template to terminal there, and tears the stack down on exit. `--self-host` forces the second mode even when a context is configured.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--template <name>` | Use an already-registered template instead of a file. Mutually exclusive with the positional `<file>`. |
| `--params <json\|@file>` | Instance params as a JSON object, or `@path` to read one from a file. |
| `--param k=v` | One param, repeatable. Merged over `--params`, later wins. `true`, `false`, integers, and floats are coerced; everything else stays a string. |
| `--instance-key <key>` | Set the new instance's `instance_key`. |
| `--tag <tag>` | Tag to attach when registering the template. |
| `--keep` | Leave the instance and template behind. On by default, remote mode only. |
| `--no-keep` | After the instance reaches terminal, delete it, undeploy the template, and delete the template. |
| `--poll-interval <duration>` | Poll interval while waiting under `--no-keep`. Defaults to `1s`. |
| `--timeout <duration>` | Maximum wait for terminal. `0` means unbounded, and is the default. |
| `--service <name>=<path>` | Bind a late-bound service to a local binary, repeatable. A bare `<name>` resolves through the alias files. |
| `--self-host` | Boot an in-process stack for this run. Incompatible with `--endpoint`. |

Plus the common flag set.

`--service` behaves differently per mode. Remotely, `run` starts the local host daemon first if `~/.rimsky/daemon.pid` names no live process. Self-hosted, it spawns each binary directly on loopback ports. A bare `--service <name>` looks the name up in the `aliases:` map of `~/.rimsky/aliases.yml` and `./.rimsky/aliases.yml`, the second overriding the first, and fails when no alias defines it.

Self-host mode rejects two combinations: `--template` needs a running rimsky, because a fresh self-hosted stack has an empty template registry, and `--keep` has nothing to keep, because the stack exits with the process.

Self-host mode writes a per-run artifact directory. It walks up from the working directory for the nearest ancestor containing a `.rimsky/` directory, falls back to the working directory, then creates `<root>/.rimsky/runs/<timestamp>-<template-name>/` and points `<root>/.rimsky/latest` at it.

### `rimsky register <file>`

Registers a template. Identical to [`rimsky template register`](#rimsky-template-register-file).

### `rimsky deploy <ref>`

Deploys a registered template. Identical to [`rimsky template deploy`](#rimsky-template-deploy-ref).

### `rimsky undeploy <ref>`

Undeploys a deployed template. Identical to [`rimsky template undeploy`](#rimsky-template-undeploy-ref).

### `rimsky instantiate <ref>`

Creates an instance. Identical to [`rimsky instance create`](#rimsky-instance-create-template-ref).

### `rimsky rm-instance <id>`

Deletes a terminal instance. Identical to [`rimsky instance delete`](#rimsky-instance-delete-id-or-key).

### `rimsky ls [templates|instances|tags]`

Lists. `ls templates` is `template list`, `ls instances` is `instance list`, `ls tags` is `tag list`. Bare `rimsky ls` lists instances, and so does `rimsky ls` followed by a flag. Any other word is refused with exit 2.

### `rimsky logs <id-or-key>`

Streams an instance's events. Identical to `instance events --follow`, and it takes that verb's flags.

### `rimsky watch <id-or-key>`

Prints a live feed of an instance's events, sorted by occurrence time, until the instance stops moving.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--until idle\|terminated` | Exit condition. `idle` means no open frame and no pending messages, confirmed over two consecutive polls. `terminated` waits for an operator-terminated instance. Defaults to `idle`. |
| `--poll-interval <duration>` | Poll interval. Defaults to `1s`. |
| `--since <RFC3339>` | Only events at or after this timestamp. |
| `--kind <kind>` | Only events of this kind. Filtered server-side. |

Plus the common flag set. `watch` exits 0 when the instance terminates, when it goes idle, or on Ctrl-C. `breakpoint.hit` events print with their checkpoint and mode.

### `rimsky health`

Reports the deployment's status and how many supervisors it sees. Takes the common flag set.

## `template`

`rimsky template <register|lint|list|get|deploy|undeploy|rm>`. All seven take the common flag set.

### `rimsky template register <file>`

Uploads the template at `<file>` and prints its hash and tags. YAML and JSON both parse. A map whose single key is `source_file` is replaced by the contents of that file, resolved relative to the template's directory; absolute paths and paths escaping the directory are refused.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--tag <tag>` | Attach this tag to the registered template. |
| `--source <text>` | Free-form source description recorded on the template. |
| `--warnings-as-errors` | Refuse registration when the validation pipeline produced any warning. |

On a 400 the verb prints the server's `validation_warnings` and `validation_errors` to stderr before the error line.

### `rimsky template lint <file>`

Validates a template and prints each warning and error as `path: message`. Prints `ok` and exits 0 when the template is clean, exits 1 when it is not.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--warnings-as-errors` | Treat warnings as findings, so any warning exits 1. |

`lint` is not an offline check: it uploads the template and the control API validates it. It needs a reachable deployment.

### `rimsky template list`

Lists templates, sorted by their alphabetically first tag, following pagination to the end.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--state <state>` | Filter by template state, server-side. |
| `--tag-prefix <prefix>` | Keep only templates carrying a tag with this prefix, filtered client-side. |

### `rimsky template get <ref>`

Prints one template's hash, state, tags, and source.

### `rimsky template deploy <ref>`

Deploys a template. Prints `<ref> deployed`, or `<ref> already deployed` when the call was a no-op.

### `rimsky template undeploy <ref>`

Undeploys a template. Prints `<ref> undeployed`, or `<ref> already undeployed`.

### `rimsky template rm <ref>`

Deregisters a template. Prints `<ref> removed`.

## `tag`

`rimsky tag <create|list|get|mv|rm>`. All five take the common flag set. All refuse a tag name starting with `compose:`.

### `rimsky tag create <tag> --template <ref>`

Points a new tag at a template. `--template` is required and accepts a hash or another tag.

### `rimsky tag list`

Lists every tag with the template hash it points at.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--prefix <prefix>` | Keep only tags with this prefix, filtered client-side. |

### `rimsky tag get <tag>`

Prints one tag's template hash and last-updated time. Exits 1 with `tag not found` when no tag matches.

### `rimsky tag mv <tag> --template <ref>`

Repoints an existing tag. `--template` is required.

### `rimsky tag rm <tag>`

Deletes a tag.

## `instance`

`rimsky instance <create|list|get|status|delete|kill|nodes|events>`. All eight take the common flag set.

### `rimsky instance create <template-ref>`

Creates an instance and prints its id, template hash, optional instance key, and node count.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--params <json\|@file>` | Instance params as a JSON object, or `@path`. |
| `--instance-key <key>` | Set the new row's `instance_key`. |
| `--daemon <silly-name>` | Target a named anonymous host daemon, overriding the local identity file. |

With no `--daemon` and no API key in play, the CLI reads or creates its local anonymous identity file and targets that daemon. With an API key present, it sends no target daemon.

### `rimsky instance list`

Lists instances as `ID`, `TEMPLATE`, `KEY`, `STATE`, following pagination to the end. `STATE` is `running` or `terminal`.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--template <hash>` | Filter by template hash, server-side. |
| `--key-prefix <prefix>` | Keep only instances whose `instance_key` has this prefix, filtered client-side. |

### `rimsky instance get <id-or-key>`

Prints one instance's id, template hash, instance key, creation time, and termination time.

### `rimsky instance status <id-or-key>`

Prints a report: the instance's identity and state, its nodes with per-node run counts, its 50 most recent events, and its pending breakpoint hits.

### `rimsky instance delete <id-or-key>`

Deletes a terminal instance and frees its instance key. Prints `<ref> deleted`.

### `rimsky instance kill <id-or-key>`

Terminates a running instance and prints its termination time, then reminds you to delete it to free the instance key.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--reason <text>` | Reason recorded on the teardown audit event. |
| `--force` | Confirm the termination. |

Without `--force` or `--yes` the verb refuses with `refusing to terminate without --force` and exits 2. It does not prompt.

### `rimsky instance nodes <id-or-key>`

Lists the instance's nodes as `ID`, `TYPE`, `RUNS`, `EXECUTOR`. `RUNS` reads `active=N pending=N fresh=N failed=N`.

### `rimsky instance events <id-or-key>`

Prints the instance's events as `occurred_at`, `id`, `kind`, following pagination to the end.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--follow` | Keep polling for new events. Ctrl-C exits 0. |
| `--poll-interval <duration>` | Poll interval under `--follow`. Defaults to `1s`. |
| `--since <RFC3339>` | Only events at or after this timestamp. |
| `--until <RFC3339>` | Only events at or before this timestamp. |

Both timestamp flags demand RFC3339. A bare date, a duration, and an epoch integer are all rejected.

## `node`

### `rimsky node get <id>`

Prints one node's id, instance id, node type, executor, and run counts. Takes the common flag set.

## `admin`

### `rimsky admin reset <node-id>`

Resets one node. The argument must be a node id — an instance id comes back `404 node not found` — and the verb demands exactly one. The control API accepts the reset only when that node has a failed terminal run in some scope, and answers 409 otherwise. Takes the common flag set, and prompts for nothing.

## `parked`

### `rimsky parked list`

Lists parked nodes as `instance`, `node_id`, `parked_at`, `resume_at`.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--older-than <duration>` | Keep only rows parked longer ago than this, filtered client-side. |
| `--instance <id>` | Keep only rows for this instance id, filtered client-side. |

Plus the common flag set.

## `messages`

`rimsky messages <tail|show>`. Both take the common flag set. Neither sends a message; the CLI has no send verb.

### `rimsky messages tail --instance <id-or-key>`

Prints an instance's messages as `id`, `type`, `sender_kind`, `sender`, `received_at`, `delivered_at`.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--instance <id-or-key>` | The instance to tail. Required. |
| `--type <type>` | Filter by message type, for example `ping/recheck`. |
| `--sender-kind <kind>` | Filter by sender kind: `operator`, `publisher`, or `instance`. |
| `--follow` | Keep polling for new messages. |
| `--poll-interval <duration>` | Poll interval under `--follow`. Defaults to `1s`. |

### `rimsky messages show <message-id>`

Prints one message's id, instance, type, sender, sender kind, timestamps, frame id, and cancelled flag.

## `asset`

`rimsky asset <list|show|versions|delete|lineage>`. All five require `--instance` and take the common flag set. `--instance` accepts a UUID or an `instance_key`.

### `rimsky asset list --instance <id-or-key>`

Lists the instance's assets as `ALIAS`, `NODE_TYPE`, `PRODUCER`, `VERSION`, `CLAIMED_AT`.

### `rimsky asset show --instance <id-or-key> <node_type>.<claim_alias>`

Prints one asset's alias, claim id, producer name, node type, version id, and claim time.

### `rimsky asset versions --instance <id-or-key> <alias>`

Lists an asset's versions as `VERSION_ID`, `COMMITTED_AT`.

### `rimsky asset delete --instance <id-or-key> <alias>`

Deletes an asset. Prints `deleted asset <alias> on instance <id>`, and prompts for nothing.

### `rimsky asset lineage --instance <id-or-key> <alias>`

Walks the asset's claim ancestors and prints them as `ID`, `KIND`, `OBSERVED_AT`, `RECORD`.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--version <version-id>` | Keep only records carrying this `version_id`, filtered client-side. |
| `--depth <n>` | Walk depth. Defaults to 3, and the server clamps anything above 50 to 50. |

This verb is a client-side composition: it resolves the alias to a claim id, then walks claim lineage. No single control-API route and no MCP tool matches it.

## `lineage`

### `rimsky lineage prune`

Deletes lineage rows older than a cutoff, and prints how many it deleted. This is the CLI's only lineage verb; the lineage query routes have no CLI verb.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--before <RFC3339>` | Delete rows observed before this timestamp. |
| `--older-than <duration>` | Shorthand: delete rows older than `now - duration`. |

One of the two is required. `--before` takes RFC3339 only. Plus the common flag set, and no prompt.

## `ctx`

`rimsky ctx <list|use|add|rm|current>` edits `~/.rimsky/config.yml`. These verbs contact no server.

### `rimsky ctx list`

Lists contexts as marker, `NAME`, `ENDPOINT`, marking the current one with `*`. Takes the common flag set; under `-o json` it prints the whole config with every `api_key` replaced by `REDACTED`.

### `rimsky ctx use <name>`

Makes an existing context current. Refuses an undefined name.

### `rimsky ctx add <name> --endpoint <url>`

Adds a context. `--endpoint` is required. Refuses a name already defined. Becomes the current context when none is set.

### `rimsky ctx rm <name>`

Removes a context. Refuses to remove the current one.

### `rimsky ctx current`

Prints the current context's name and endpoint, tab-separated. Exits 1 when no context is current.

## `auth`

`rimsky auth <init|login|create-key|list|show|revoke|rotate|status>`. Every subcommand except `login` takes `--endpoint` and `--key`, and no other common flag.

### `rimsky auth init`

Mints the deployment's first admin key while it is still in anonymous mode, and prints the plaintext once. Refuses with exit 1 when the deployment already reports itself authenticated.

### `rimsky auth login`

Prompts for a control-API URL and an API key on the terminal, verifies them against `GET /v1/auth/status`, and writes both to the active context. Reads the key without echo when stdin is a terminal. Takes no flags and no arguments.

### `rimsky auth create-key --name <name> {--role <role>|--role-file <path>}`

Mints an API key and prints the plaintext once.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--name <name>` | Name for the new key. Required. |
| `--role <role>` | Bundled role: `admin`, `agent-supervisor`, `debug-operator`, `operator`, `publisher-service`, or `read-only`. |
| `--role-file <path>` | Load the role from a JSON file instead. |
| `--add <action>` | Append a grant entry for this action, repeatable. |
| `--remove <action>` | Drop grant entries naming this action, repeatable. |
| `--expires <duration>` | Lifetime for the key, for example `24h` or `30d`. |

One of `--role` or `--role-file` is required. The CLI expands the role into its grant locally, before it contacts the server, so an unknown role name fails without a reachable deployment. `--add` validates each action string against the action registry; wildcards are limited to `*`, `<noun>:*`, and `*:<verb>`.

### `rimsky auth list`

Lists keys as `NAME`, `ID`, `ROLE`, `CREATED`, `LAST_USED`. The `ROLE` column is a client-side match: the CLI compares each key's grant against the six bundled roles and prints `role:<name>` on an exact match, `custom` otherwise.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--name-filter <glob>` | Filter by key name, server-side. |
| `--include-revoked` | Include revoked rows. |
| `--json` | Print the raw key rows as JSON. |

### `rimsky auth show <name-or-id>`

Prints one key's stored row as JSON: `id`, `name`, `permissions`, `created_at`, `created_by_key_id`, `last_used_at`. It never returns key material.

### `rimsky auth revoke <name-or-id>`

Revokes a key and prints `revoked key "<name>"`. Prompts for nothing.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--force-leave-anonymous` | Allow a revocation that drops the deployment to zero active keys. |

Revoking the last active key without that flag answers 409.

### `rimsky auth rotate <name-or-id>`

Mints a replacement key under the same name and grant, prints the new plaintext once, and prints when the old key stops working.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--grace <duration>` | How long the old key keeps working. Defaults to `24h`. The server parses it. |

Rotation is how you recover from a lost key: the name and the grant survive, the original secret does not.

### `rimsky auth status`

Prints the deployment's auth mode and key counts. Reports `anonymous` while the key ledger is empty and `authenticated` once a key exists.

## `daemon`

`rimsky daemon <start|status|stop>` manages the local host daemon. These subcommands take neither `--endpoint` nor `--key`.

### `rimsky daemon start`

Starts the host daemon, daemonized by default, and waits for it to report a live connection to the proxy before returning. Prints `rimsky daemon started (pid N, connected to <proxy>)`. Exits 1 when the daemon dies or fails to connect within 10 seconds, naming `~/.rimsky/daemon.log`.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--proxy <host:port>` | Host-daemon-proxy endpoint. Required, unless `RIMSKY_HOST_DAEMON_PROXY_URL` supplies it. |
| `--api-key <plaintext>` | Key plaintext presented to the proxy on `Register`. Omit to register anonymously. Overrides `RIMSKY_API_KEY`. |
| `--listen <addr>` | Local listener address. Defaults to `127.0.0.1:0`. |
| `--allow-paths <globs>` | Comma-separated glob patterns for validating spawnable binary paths. |
| `--tls` | Dial the proxy over TLS. Overrides `RIMSKY_DAEMON_TLS`. |
| `--tls-ca <path>` | Pinned deployment CA root PEM verifying the proxy's server certificate. Overrides `RIMSKY_DAEMON_TLS_CA`. |
| `--label <silly-name>` | Anonymous routing label the daemon asks the proxy to adopt. Meaningful only without `--api-key`. |
| `--identity-file <path>` | Anonymous identity JSON file. Defaults to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rimsky/host-daemon/identity.json`. |
| `--state-dir <dir>` | Directory for the pid, status, and log files. Defaults to `~/.rimsky`. |
| `--foreground` | Run in the foreground instead of daemonizing. |

### `rimsky daemon status`

Reports whether the daemon runs, its pid, the proxy it connected to, since when, and its spawned children. Prints `rimsky daemon: not running` and exits 0 when no live pid file exists. Takes `--state-dir`.

### `rimsky daemon stop`

Sends SIGTERM, waits, escalates to SIGKILL if needed, then removes the pid and status files. Prints `rimsky daemon: stopped (pid N)`. Takes `--state-dir`.

## `compose`

`rimsky compose <up|down|plan|status|run>` drives a `rimsky-compose.yml` manifest.

`up`, `down`, `plan`, and `status` reconcile the manifest against an already-running rimsky. All four take `-f` and the common flag set.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-f`, `--f <path>` | Manifest path. Defaults to `rimsky-compose.yml`. |

These four verbs reject positional arguments. When the manifest pins a `context:`, that context decides the endpoint.

### `rimsky compose up`

Computes a plan and applies it. Before applying, it prints every destructive step and asks `Proceed? [y/N]` on stderr; `--yes` skips the question. Prints `applied N changes`, or `no changes`.

### `rimsky compose down`

Removes everything the manifest's project owns. Prompts the same way, and `--yes` skips it. Prints `compose down complete`.

### `rimsky compose plan`

Prints the changes `up` would apply, and mutates nothing. Exits 0 when the world already matches, and 3 when the plan carries changes or drift warnings.

### `rimsky compose status`

Prints each tag and instance the project touches as `KIND`, `NAME`, `ANNOTATION`, where the annotation reads `in-manifest`, `manifest-missing-from-api`, or `api-missing-from-manifest`.

### `rimsky compose run <manifest>`

Boots an in-process all-in-one stack, drives the manifest's instances to terminal, then tears the stack down. Takes exactly one positional manifest and none of the common flags.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--name <name>` | Run name appended to the artifact directory. Defaults to the manifest's project. |
| `--workdir <dir>` | Artifact root, suppressing the walk-up discovery. |
| `--timeout <duration>` | Maximum wall-clock duration. `0` means unbounded, and is the default. |
| `--quiet` | Suppress per-instance progress; print only the final summary. |
| `--verbose` | Include frame ticks and claim events in the progress output. |
| `--json` | Emit progress as JSON Lines on stderr. |
| `--service <name>=<path>` | Bind a late-bound service to a local binary, repeatable. |

`--quiet` and `--verbose` are mutually exclusive. Progress goes to stderr in every mode, JSON included. The verb writes its artifacts to `<root>/.rimsky/runs/<timestamp>-<name>/`.

## `conformance`

`rimsky conformance <executor|claim-producer|publisher|validation|data-processing|lifecycle-subscriber|probe>` proves a third-party implementation against a protocol. Each subcommand parses its own flags, prints one `ok` or `FAIL` line per check, and closes with `N/M checks failed` when anything failed.

Every subcommand exits 0 on a clean run, 1 on any failure, and 2 on a usage error. A failed check and an unreachable endpoint both exit 1.

### `rimsky conformance executor --endpoint <url>`

Runs the executor scenario suite.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--endpoint <url>` | Executor or lifecycle service endpoint. Required. |
| `--transport grpc` | Transport. `grpc` is the only accepted value. |
| `--tls off\|required` | Dial with TLS verified against system roots. Defaults to `off`. |
| `--allow-live` | Run against a live, non-stub endpoint; stub-requiring scenarios skip instead of refusing the run. |
| `--scenarios <a,b,c>` | Run only these scenarios. |
| `--skip <a,b,c>` | Skip these scenarios. |
| `--timeout <duration>` | Per-scenario timeout. Defaults to `30s`. |
| `--check-observability` | Additionally probe the executor-observability protocol. |
| `--retention-test-seconds <n>` | With a positive value, drive a dispatch, sleep that many seconds, and verify the trace reports itself evicted. Takes a bare integer, not a duration. |
| `--callback-bind <host>` | Interface the callback receiver binds. Defaults to `127.0.0.1`; use `0.0.0.0` for a containerized executor. |
| `--callback-host <host>` | Host the executor should dial the receiver at. Defaults to `--callback-bind`. |

A run where every scenario skipped exits 1 and says coverage was not verified — unless `--allow-live` is set and the stub gate caused every skip, which exits 0 with the same warning in words.

### `rimsky conformance claim-producer --endpoint <url>`

Runs the claim-producer checks.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--endpoint <url>` | Claim-producer endpoint. Required. A bare `http(s)` base URL under `--transport http`. |
| `--transport grpc\|http` | Transport. Defaults to `grpc`. |
| `--timeout <duration>` | Per-check timeout. Defaults to `10s`. |
| `--check-observability` | Additionally probe claim-producer-observability. Requires `--transport grpc`. |
| `--retention-test-seconds <n>` | Drive a claim, sleep, and verify the claim reports itself evicted. |

### `rimsky conformance publisher --endpoint <url> --kind <kind>`

Runs the publisher checks.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--endpoint <url>` | Publisher gRPC endpoint. Required. |
| `--kind <kind>` | Publisher kind to exercise, for example `cron`, `http`, `object-store`, `webhook`. Required. |
| `--transport grpc` | Transport. `grpc` is the only accepted value. |
| `--resolved-config <json>` | Kind-specific `resolved_config` passed to `Subscribe`. |
| `--instance-id <id>` | Instance id passed to `Subscribe`. |
| `--message-type <type>` | Message type passed to `Subscribe` and watched for. Defaults to `system/conformance`. |
| `--control-api <url>` | Control-API base URL to poll for the publisher's pushed message. Enables the message-push check together with `--instance-id`. Overrides `RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_URL`. |
| `--timeout <duration>` | Per-suite timeout. Defaults to `30s`. |

### `rimsky conformance validation --endpoint <url>`

Runs the validation checks.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--endpoint <url>` | Validation service gRPC endpoint. Required. |
| `--role <role>` | Role to validate against: `executor`, `claim_producer`, `lifecycle_subscriber`, or `publisher`. Defaults to `executor`. |
| `--transport grpc` | Transport. `grpc` is the only accepted value. |
| `--timeout <duration>` | Per-suite timeout. Defaults to `30s`. |

### `rimsky conformance data-processing --endpoint <url>`

Runs the data-processing checks. Takes `--endpoint` (required), `--transport grpc`, and `--timeout`, defaulting to `30s`.

### `rimsky conformance lifecycle-subscriber --endpoint <url>`

Runs the lifecycle-subscriber check. Takes `--endpoint` (required), `--transport grpc`, `--tls off|required`, and `--timeout`, defaulting to `30s`. Prints `lifecycle-subscriber: ok`.

### `rimsky conformance probe --endpoint <url>`

Asks one executor whether it answers in stub mode, and nothing else. Takes `--endpoint` (required), `--transport grpc`, `--timeout` defaulting to `15s`, `--callback-bind`, and `--callback-host`. Prints `conformance: stub-mode probe OK`.

## `version` and `help`

`rimsky version`, `rimsky --version`, and `rimsky -v` print `rimsky <version>` and exit 0. They ignore everything after them.

`rimsky help`, `rimsky --help`, and `rimsky -h` print the root usage to stdout and exit 0. The same three forms on a family node — `rimsky template --help`, `rimsky auth --help` — print that family's subcommand list to stdout and exit 0.

## Flag index

Every flag the CLI defines, with the verbs that take it. Flags whose names repeat across families mean different things in each; the table separates those meanings.

| Flag | Verbs | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--add` | `auth create-key` | Append a grant entry, repeatable. |
| `--daemon` | `instance create`, `instantiate` | Target anonymous host daemon by routing label. |
| `--allow-live` | `conformance executor` | Permit a non-stub endpoint; stub scenarios skip. |
| `--allow-paths` | `daemon start` | Comma-separated globs for binary path validation. |
| `--api-key` | `daemon start` | Key plaintext the daemon presents to the proxy. |
| `--before` | `lineage prune` | RFC3339 cutoff for deletion. |
| `--callback-bind` | `conformance executor`, `conformance probe` | Interface the callback receiver binds. |
| `--callback-host` | `conformance executor`, `conformance probe` | Host the executor dials the receiver at. |
| `--check-observability` | `conformance executor`, `conformance claim-producer` | Also probe the observability sibling protocol. |
| `--control-api` | `conformance publisher` | Control API to poll for the pushed message. |
| `--depth` | `asset lineage` | Walk depth. Defaults to 3, clamped at 50. |
| `--endpoint` | Every common-flag verb, every `auth` subcommand except `login`, `ctx add` | Control-API URL. On `ctx add`, the endpoint stored on the new context. |
| `--expires` | `auth create-key` | Key lifetime, for example `24h` or `30d`. |
| `-f`, `--f` | `compose up\|down\|plan\|status` | Manifest path. Defaults to `rimsky-compose.yml`. |
| `--follow` | `instance events`, `messages tail` | Keep polling. |
| `--force` | `instance kill` | Confirm the termination. |
| `--force-leave-anonymous` | `auth revoke` | Permit dropping to zero active keys. |
| `--foreground` | `daemon start` | Do not daemonize. |
| `--grace` | `auth rotate` | How long the old key keeps working. Defaults to `24h`. |
| `--identity-file` | `daemon start` | Anonymous identity JSON file. |
| `--include-revoked` | `auth list` | Include revoked rows. |
| `--instance` | `asset *`, `messages tail`, `parked list` | The instance to act on or filter by. |
| `--instance-id` | `conformance publisher` | Instance id passed to `Subscribe`. |
| `--instance-key` | `instance create`, `instantiate`, `run` | Instance key for the new row. |
| `--json` | `auth list` | Print rows as JSON on stdout. |
| `--json` | `compose run` | Emit progress as JSON Lines on stderr. |
| `--keep` | `run` | Leave instance and template behind. On by default. |
| `--key` | Every common-flag verb, every `auth` subcommand except `login` | API key sent as a bearer token. |
| `--key-prefix` | `instance list`, `ls instances` | Client-side filter on instance key. |
| `--kind` | `watch` | Server-side event-kind filter. |
| `--kind` | `conformance publisher` | Publisher kind to exercise. |
| `--label` | `daemon start` | Anonymous routing label to adopt. |
| `--listen` | `daemon start` | Local listener address. |
| `--message-type` | `conformance publisher` | Message type to subscribe and watch for. |
| `--name` | `auth create-key` | Name for the new key. Required. |
| `--name` | `compose run` | Run name in the artifact directory. |
| `--name-filter` | `auth list` | Server-side glob on key name. |
| `--no-color` | Every common-flag verb | Suppress ANSI color. |
| `--no-keep` | `run` | Clean up instance and template after terminal. |
| `-o`, `--o`, `--output` | Every common-flag verb | Output format: `human` or `json`. |
| `--older-than` | `lineage prune` | Delete rows older than `now - duration`. |
| `--older-than` | `parked list` | Keep rows parked longer ago than this. |
| `--param` | `run` | One `k=v` param, repeatable, merged over `--params`. |
| `--params` | `run`, `instance create`, `instantiate` | Params as a JSON object or `@file`. |
| `--poll-interval` | `run`, `instance events`, `logs`, `messages tail`, `watch` | Poll interval. Defaults to `1s`. |
| `--prefix` | `tag list`, `ls tags` | Client-side filter on tag prefix. |
| `--proxy` | `daemon start` | Host-daemon-proxy endpoint. |
| `--quiet` | `compose run` | Only the final summary. |
| `--reason` | `instance kill` | Reason on the teardown audit event. |
| `--remove` | `auth create-key` | Drop grant entries naming this action, repeatable. |
| `--resolved-config` | `conformance publisher` | JSON `resolved_config` for `Subscribe`. |
| `--retention-test-seconds` | `conformance executor`, `conformance claim-producer` | Bare integer seconds for the eviction check. |
| `--role` | `auth create-key` | Bundled role name. |
| `--role` | `conformance validation` | Role to validate against. |

| `--scenarios` | `conformance executor` | Comma-list of scenarios to run. |

| `--tag` | `template register`, `register`, `run` | Tag to attach at registration. |
| `--tag-prefix` | `template list`, `ls templates` | Client-side filter on attached tags. |
| `--template` | `tag create`, `tag mv` | Template ref the tag points at. Required. |
| `--template` | `instance list`, `ls instances` | Server-side filter by template hash. |
| `--template` | `run` | Name of an already-registered template. |
| `--timeout` | `run`, `compose run` | Maximum wall-clock wait. `0` means unbounded. |
| `--timeout` | Every `conformance` subcommand | Per-check or per-scenario timeout. |
| `--tls` | `daemon start` | Boolean: dial the proxy over TLS. |
| `--tls` | `conformance executor`, `conformance lifecycle-subscriber` | `off` or `required`. |
| `--tls-ca` | `daemon start` | Pinned CA root PEM for the proxy's certificate. |
| `--transport` | Every `conformance` subcommand | `grpc`, plus `http` on `claim-producer`. |
| `--type` | `messages tail` | Filter by message type. |
| `--until` | `instance events`, `logs` | Only events at or before this RFC3339 timestamp. |
| `--until` | `watch` | Exit condition: `idle` or `terminated`. |
| `--verbose` | `compose run` | Include frame ticks and claim events. |
| `--version` | `asset lineage` | Keep only records carrying this version id. |
| `--warnings-as-errors` | `template register`, `register`, `template lint` | Treat validation warnings as failures. |
| `--workdir` | `compose run` | Artifact root override. |
| `--yes` | Every common-flag verb | Stands in for `--force` on `instance kill`; answers the compose prompt. |

## Environment variables

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_URL` | Control-API URL, below `--endpoint` and above the config file. |
| `RIMSKY_API_KEY` | API key, below `--key` and above the context's stored key. |
| `RIMSKY_CONTEXT` | Selects a context by name, overriding `current_context`. |
| `NO_COLOR` | Any non-empty value disables ANSI color. |

`rimsky daemon start` reads the host daemon's own variables, and each of its flags overrides the matching one: `RIMSKY_HOST_DAEMON_PROXY_URL`, `RIMSKY_API_KEY`, `RIMSKY_DAEMON_LISTEN`, `RIMSKY_DAEMON_ALLOW_PATHS`, `RIMSKY_DAEMON_TLS`, `RIMSKY_DAEMON_TLS_CA`, and the identity-file and routing-label variables.

## Where the CLI will surprise you

Each item below is a reasonable expectation the CLI does not meet, and what it does instead.

**No verb takes `--dry-run`.** The control API serves a per-request dry-run mode, but no CLI verb exposes it under `--dry-run`, `--preview`, or `-n`; all three are parse errors on every write verb. `rimsky compose plan` is the only preview on offer, and it covers the compose family alone. If a key's grant pins an action to `dry_run`, the write is previewed server-side and the CLI still prints `<hash> deployed` and exits 0 — under `-o json` it prints `{}`. Do not read a CLI success as proof the write landed when the key is scoped that way.

**Destructive verbs do not prompt, outside the compose family.** `tag rm`, `template rm`, `instance delete`, `rm-instance`, `undeploy`, `auth revoke`, `admin reset`, `lineage prune`, `asset delete`, and `instance kill --force` all destroy their subject immediately, even on a terminal with input waiting. `--yes` answers no question on any of them: it exists as a common flag and, on `instance kill`, it enables the destruction rather than confirming one. `compose up` and `compose down` are the only verbs that ask, and there `--yes` really does skip the prompt.

**`--json` is not the JSON flag.** Exactly one verb takes `--json` for JSON output: `rimsky auth list`. Every other read verb rejects it and exits 2 with an empty stdout, so `rimsky ls templates --json | jq` prints nothing and fails. The control-API verbs spell it `-o json`, and `auth list` is precisely the verb that will not take `-o json`. The two spellings sit on disjoint verb sets. `compose run --json` is a third meaning: JSON Lines on **stderr**, with stdout left empty.

**`-o` accepts four words and honours two.** `-o human` and `-o json` work. `-o yaml` is rejected. `-o table` and `-o text` are accepted and silently mean `human`, so asking for a table gets you no error and no table.

**Short flags barely exist.** `-o` is a real short form of `--output`. `-f` is not `--follow` or `--force`: every verb carrying those long flags rejects `-f`, and the only `-f` in the product is the compose manifest path. `-v` prints the version at the root and is a parse error one word to the right, as in `rimsky ls templates -v`. `--yes` has no `-y`. Short flags do not cluster and take no attached value; `-o=json` works, `-ojson` does not.

**`--help` exits 2 on a leaf verb.** The root and the family nodes exit 0. Every leaf — `rimsky conformance executor --help`, `rimsky instance list --help` — prints its usage to **stderr** and exits 2. A `set -e` wrapper around a help call fails, and a script reading a non-zero status as "no such verb" is wrong about most of the tree. Six dev-loop shortcuts print the grouped verb's usage rather than their own: `rimsky rm-instance --help` prints "Usage of instance delete". `rimsky version --help` ignores the flag and prints the version.

**The compose family drops your credential.** `compose up`, `down`, `plan`, and `status` accept `--key` and read `RIMSKY_API_KEY`, then send the request without an `Authorization` header. Against any deployment that has left anonymous mode, they answer `401 unauthorized` and nothing warns you that the credential was discarded. The compose family works only against an anonymous-mode deployment at this release.

**Time-window flags are not uniform.** `--since` reaches three time-ordered reads, `--until` three, `--older-than` two, `--before` one. `messages tail` defines neither `--since` nor `--until`. The sharpest edge is `watch --until`, which names an exit condition, not an upper bound: `rimsky watch <id> --until 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z` fails with `--until must be idle or terminated`, while the same flag on `instance events` takes exactly that timestamp. Where the flags do accept a timestamp, the grammar is RFC3339 and nothing else.

**Duration flags do not share one grammar.** Most duration flags — `--poll-interval`, `--older-than`, `--timeout` — take Go's duration syntax, so `30s`, `5m`, `24h`, `1h30m`, and `500ms` parse and `30d` and `1w` do not. `auth create-key --expires` is the exception and accepts `30d`. Its sibling `auth rotate --grace` rejects `30d`, and rejects it server-side as `400 invalid grace duration`. `--retention-test-seconds` takes a bare integer and rejects `30s` outright.

**Half the control API has no CLI verb.** The CLI reaches roughly half the declared control-API routes. Missing entirely: the breakpoint debugger and debug override, `instance pause` and `instance resume`, every lineage query route (the CLI ships only the `lineage prune` write), every observability route, the audit log, `auth whoami`, the run-detail route, enrollment and CA-root, the MCP transport routes, the admin diagnostics beyond parked nodes, and message *sending* — the CLI can tail and show messages but cannot post one. Reach for HTTP for those.

**`template lint` needs a live deployment.** The verb uploads the template and the control API validates it, so `rimsky template lint <file>` with nothing reachable fails with `connection refused`. This is structural, not incidental: the findings name the deployment's own `executors:` and `claim_producers:` blocks, so the same file can lint clean against one deployment and fail against another. CI with no deployment cannot lint. Lint does catch everything registration rejects, on every defect measured.

**`auth show` never returns key material.** Neither `auth show` nor `auth list` nor the underlying route returns a key's plaintext; the server stores a digest. The plaintext appears exactly once, in the response to the mint. Recover a lost key with `auth rotate`, which prints a new plaintext, keeps the name and the grant, and retires the old secret when the grace passes.

**Roles live in the CLI, not the server.** `--role operator` is expanded into its grant before the CLI contacts the server, so an unknown role name fails without a reachable deployment. The server stores grants and knows nothing of role names: no route lists roles, and a key's row carries no role field. The `ROLE` column in `auth list` is a client-side match against the six bundled grants — a key created over HTTP with the same grant lists as that role, and a bundled role patched with `--add` lists as `custom`.

**Permission wildcards are not globs.** A grant action accepts `*`, `<noun>:*`, and `*:<verb>` and nothing else. `instance:re*`, `*:re*`, `instance:**`, and `*:*` are all refused at key creation with `unsupported wildcard shape`. A wildcard also skips the action-registry check, so `banana:*` mints a key that authorizes nothing, while the literal `banana:read` is refused outright.

**`admin reset` resets one node and nothing else.** The argument must be a node id; an instance id answers `404 node not found`. The control API accepts the reset only when that node has a failed terminal run in some scope, and answers 409 otherwise. It is not a deployment wipe, and it does not confirm.

**Anonymous mode has no off switch.** No configuration key and no environment variable disables it. The deployment reports `anonymous` while its key ledger is empty and flips to `authenticated` the moment `rimsky auth init` mints the first key. Until then it accepts unauthenticated requests, and prints a WARN banner saying so.

**Asset operations do not match across surfaces.** `rimsky asset lineage` is CLI-only: no control-API route and no MCP tool matches it, and it is a client-side composition that fails on the asset lookup before it reaches any lineage call. The reverse gap also exists — asset materialization history has a route and an MCP tool but no CLI verb, and `rimsky asset materialization-history` is refused. List, show, versions, and delete do appear on all three surfaces.

**Conformance output is text, and one exit code covers every runtime outcome.** No conformance subcommand accepts `--json` or `--warnings-as-errors`, so CI must parse the printed `ok` / `FAIL` rows and the closing `N/M checks failed` line. A failed check, an unreachable endpoint, and an unopenable backend all exit 1; only a usage error is distinct, at 2. A CI job reading the status alone cannot tell "your implementation failed" from "I never reached your endpoint". There is also no `conformance host-daemon` subcommand: nothing in the kit proves a host-daemon implementation. Executor-observability and claim-producer-observability have no subcommand either, but `--check-observability` on their siblings covers both.
